title: बैतडेली भाषाका व्यतिरेकी वर्णको पहिचान र वितरण
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख बैतडेली भाषाका व्यतिरेकी वर्णसँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । यसको मुख्य उद्देश्य बैतडेली भाषाका व्यतिरेकी वर्णको पहिचान गरी तिनको वितरण अवस्था पत्ता लगाउनु रहेको छ । यसमा मुख्यगरी स्थलगत अध्ययन र आंशिक रूपमा शीर्षकसँग सम्बन्धित द्वितीय सामग्रीको उपयोग गरी प्राप्त तथ्यको गुणात्मक ढाँचामा व्याख्या विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । वर्ण पहिचान र विश्लेषणका लागि व्यतिरेकी विश्लेषण र वितरणलाई मुख्य आधार मानिएको छ । बैतडेली भाषामा ६ ओटा ह्रस्व स्वर र तिनका दीर्घ रूप गरी १२ ओटा स्वर वर्ण र ३० ओटा व्यतिरेकी व्यञ्जन वर्ण रहेका छन् । तिनमा /ण्/ पदादि र /घ्, ढ्, ध्, भ्, य्, व्, ह्/ पदान्तमा वितरण नभएको देखिन्छ भने कण्ठ्य नासिक्य /ङ्/ पदादिमा सीमित अनुकरणात्मक शब्दमा मात्र र वत्स्र्य स्पर्श /ढ्/ पदमध्यमा सीमित रूपमा मात्र वितरण भएको पाइन्छ । अन्य स्वर तथा व्यञ्जन वर्णहरू पदादि, पदमध्य र पदान्तमा वितरित भएको पाइएको छ । त्यसैगरी अल्पप्राण, वत्स्र्य स्पर्शी /ड्/ पदादि र द्वित्व हुँदा पदमध्यमा वितरित भएको पाइएको छ भने अन्य अवस्थामा मूर्धन्य ताडित /ड्Þ/ मा परिवर्तित भएको पाइएको छ । त्यसैले /ड्/ र /ड्Þ/ लाई छुट्टै वर्ण नमानी क्रमशः /ड्/ वर्णको संवर्ण मान्न सकिने निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । खण्डेतर वर्णमा अनुनासिकता र मात्रा बैतडेली भाषामा व्यतिरेकी देखिएका छन् ।
american_english: The present article is concerned with the contrastive phonemes of the Baitadeli language. Its primary objective is to identify the contrastive phonemes of the Baitadeli language and ascertain their distributional status. In this, utilizing primarily field study and partially secondary materials related to the topic, an explanation and analysis of the acquired facts is carried out in a qualitative framework. Contrastive analysis and distribution are taken as the primary basis for phoneme identification and analysis. In the Baitadeli language, there are 12 vowel phonemes, comprising 6 short vowels and their long forms, and 30 contrastive consonant phonemes. Among them, /ṇ/ appears not to be distributed word-initially and /gh, ḍh, dh, bh, y, v, h/ word-finally, whereas the velar nasal /ṅ/ is found distributed word-initially only in limited onomatopoeic words and the alveolar plosive /ḍh/ word-medially only to a limited extent. Other vowel and consonant phonemes are found to be distributed word-initially, word-medially, and word-finally. Likewise, the unaspirated alveolar plosive /ḍ/ is found to be distributed word-initially and, when geminated, word-medially, whereas in other environments it is found to change into the retroflex flap /ṛ/. Therefore, rather than considering /ḍ/ and /ṛ/ as distinct phonemes, the conclusion is drawn that they can be regarded as allophones of the phoneme /ḍ/. Among suprasegmental features, nasality and length are observed to be contrastive in the Baitadeli language.

australian_english: This article is concerned with the contrastive phonemes of the Baitadeli language. Its main objective is to identify the contrastive phonemes of the Baitadeli language and work out their distribution. In this, using mainly field study and partly secondary materials related to the topic, an explanation and analysis of the findings is carried out within a qualitative framework. Contrastive analysis and distribution are taken as the main basis for phoneme identification and analysis. In the Baitadeli language, there are 12 vowel phonemes, made up of 6 short vowels and their long forms, and 30 contrastive consonant phonemes. Among them, /ṇ/ does not seem to be distributed word-initially and /gh, ḍh, dh, bh, y, v, h/ word-finally, while the velar nasal /ṅ/ is found distributed word-initially only in a few onomatopoeic words and the alveolar plosive /ḍh/ word-medially only in a limited way. Other vowel and consonant phonemes are found to be distributed word-initially, word-medially and word-finally. In the same way, the unaspirated alveolar plosive /ḍ/ is found to be distributed word-initially and, when geminated, word-medially, while in other environments it is found to turn into the retroflex flap /ṛ/. Therefore, rather than treating /ḍ/ and /ṛ/ as separate phonemes, the conclusion is drawn that they can be seen as allophones of the phoneme /ḍ/. Among suprasegmental features, nasality and vowel length are seen to be contrastive in the Baitadeli language.
